rationale.overall: B reads as a lit solid the way the REFERENCE does — continuous form shading and a warm falloff across the slab — whereas A reads as flat panels with drawn creases, so B wins despite A holding its edges better.
rationale.material: B has the volumetric gradient, subtle surface mottling and soft translucency along the top face that the REFERENCE's stone shows, while A is a near-uniform dark fill with a hard facet line and outline strokes the REFERENCE never has.
rationale.silhouette: A keeps a crisp, evenly contrasted outline against the two-tone ground, while B's upper-right corner lightens toward the background and softens the block's boundary there.
rationale.smallsize: At 32px and 16px A stays a compact dark bar with a decisive orange underline, whereas B's lighter top end blurs into the pale field and the mass reads slightly mushier.
